bull_case: If Zero Trust Exchange sustains high-teens organic growth, Red Canary expands SecOps attach, and SBC falls materially as a share of revenue, owner FCF/share can approach the Bull path and support value above $350.
bear_case: If organic ARR growth settles in the mid-teens while SBC remains structurally high and infrastructure capex stays elevated, owner FCF/share may normalize far below the level embedded in the current price.
thesis: At $197.31, ZS trades at about 1.216x the locked Base DCF of $162.29. The valuation therefore requires execution somewhat above Base but below Bull. The more important issue is cash-flow quality: FY2026 company FCF was $779.1M, but SBC of $821.9M means owner-style FCF after SBC was roughly breakeven.

evidence.claim: FY2026 OCF was $1.129654B, capex/other asset purchases $277.304M, capitalized internal-use software $73.207M and SBC $821.923M.
FY2027 revenue growth guidance is 16.6%-17.5% and ARR growth guidance 16.6%-17.4%.
Locked Bear/Base/Bull values are about $45.41/$162.29/$352.64; price/Base is ~1.216.

counterevidence: Zero Trust architecture has secular tailwinds from cloud, AI agents and perimeter collapse.
Net cash is substantial and RPO provides multi-year revenue visibility.
unknowns: Normalized SBC as a percentage of revenue over the next 3-5 years
Red Canary cross-sell economics and organic ARR contribution
Long-run infrastructure intensity as AI security workloads scale
falsifiers: If owner FCF/share grows materially faster than the Base path while SBC/revenue declines, the valuation concern weakens.
If organic ARR growth falls below mid-teens and SBC remains above 20% of revenue, the valuation concern strengthens.
